newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares drift lower on sales of blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares drift lower on sales of blue chips.

text.p: Italian shares closed mostly lower on Monday, driven down by institutional selling of shares in energy group ENI, telecoms company Telecom Italia and Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM).
The all-share mibtel index finished 0.93 percent down at 12,680 while the blue chip mib30 index ended 1.09 percent lower at 18,893.

Heavy foreign buying drove up selected Italian banks, including Banca Commerciale Italiana and Credito Italiano, which finished 4.06 percent and 2.74 percent higher, respectively, at 3,790 lire and 2,510 lire.
Banca di Roma was also very well bought, with orders partly driven by rumours that it might be considering the sale of Banca Nazionale dell'Agricoltura, which also made strong gains.
Banca di Roma ended the day 5.3 percent higher at 1,431 lire with BNA putting on 6.4 percent to finish 1,280 lire.
Brokers said that fund managers were attracted to banks with strong fund management operations, hence the interest in BCI and Credito.
Insurance companies were neglected, Generali shedding 1.71 percent to close at 33,548 lire and Alleanza closing 0.79 percent down at 12,802 lire.
Shares in TIM were pushed lower by investors who had become overweight in the stock.
Analysts said it appeared the market needed to consolidate after making very strong gains in January.
